sections.html:
The state capital is also the Lewis and Clark County seat. At the 2020 count it had 32,091 people in about 17 square miles, and 83,058 lived in the metro area spanning Lewis and Clark and Jefferson counties. Helena fills part of the Helena Valley, Tenmile Creek crosses it, and hillside neighborhoods climb the edges. On a hillside lot a buyer weighs the slope, the access road and fire exposure.

Public employers carry the local economy: about 18 percent of working Helenans hold state agency jobs, and county, federal, school and medical employers fill out the rest. Many buyers come from those fields. Sellers who relocate, retire or inherit tend to want a closing date they can count on. Parts of town have Victorian homes from the gold camp years, which some buyers love and others fear.

Little rain or snow reaches Helena, just 11.4 inches a year, most of it in spring, yet winters are long and cold and summers hot. Recorded temperatures run from 105 degrees Fahrenheit down to minus 42. Roof, siding and foundation all get a hard look from inspectors because of that range.

The city's zoning code says its regulations seek to minimize danger from wildland fires, stormwater flooding, soil erosion and other environmental hazards, to mitigate traffic hazards and to protect the scenic character of hillside areas. Chapter 2 of Title 11 of the Helena City Code sets out the land uses allowed in each district.

The same chapter covers accessory dwelling units. Only a single-dwelling unit residence may have one, and only one per lot, with a detached or attached ADU capped at 75 percent of the main house or 1,000 square feet, whichever comes first. A garage apartment or converted basement should be checked with the city for a permit and for fit within those limits, since an unpermitted unit must be disclosed.

A simple checklist for a sale:

  • Look up your lot's zoning district on the city planning pages.
  • Find permits for additions, finished basements and any second unit.
  • Note any hillside, drainage or access issues you know of.
  • Collect records for roof, furnace and chimney work.

The City of Helena's Community Development Department handles this. Its Building Division reviews building and site plans, issues building permits and does inspections within city limits, and Historic Preservation sits in the same department.

If you remodeled without permits, a buyer may ask the city for records, and a missing permit can slow a deal. Montana's disclosure law asks sellers to say whether substantial additions or alterations were made without a building permit. Deal with that before the contract rather than after.

sections.h2: How and when Helena property tax is paid
sections.html:
Roughly 37,000 real estate tax bills a year go out from Lewis and Clark County. They are mailed by the treasurer in late October, with the first payment due November 30 (or within 30 days of the postmark, whichever comes later) and the second due May 31.

Tax questionWhere to go
PaymentsLewis and Clark County, 316 North Park Avenue, Room 113, Helena
Property tax office phone406-447-8329
First half dueNovember 30, or 30 days after the postmark if later
Second half dueMay 31
ADU size limitOne per lot, up to 75% of the main house or 1,000 sq ft

The title company takes whatever tax is owed for the current period out of your proceeds at closing.

sections.h2: What a Montana seller must disclose
sections.html:
Helena sellers owe buyers a written list of known adverse material facts. Under section 70-20-502 of the Montana Code that covers title, water and wastewater, utilities, structural and mechanical systems, soil and drainage, and radon, mold, lead-based paint or contaminated soil testing. A statement handed over after the contract is signed gives the buyer three days to rescind (section 70-20-504).

Section 70-20-503 carves out court-ordered transfers like probate, foreclosure sales, and transfers to a spouse, child or parent.

• Agent listing. Full market exposure, along with showings, a buyer's inspection and a buyer's loan.
  • Owner sale. No commission. You run the buyer, the contract and the disclosure.
  • Cash offer. As is, with no loan approval to wait for. Condition is priced in, so get it in writing and compare your net.

Whichever you pick, ask for payoff statements on your mortgage and any liens, plus a closing cost estimate, to see what remains.

sections.h2: Hillside and wildfire questions buyers ask
sections.html: Because the zoning code names wildland fire and hillside character as concerns, buyers of homes on slopes often ask about access for fire crews, drainage and erosion, and how well the lot is cleared. Have answers ready. Clear dry brush and woodpiles, note any retaining walls or drainage work you have done, and keep your roof and chimney records together. Ask your insurer for a written statement of current coverage, because a buyer may want to see it. None of this requires spending money before a sale, but a seller who has the facts ready tends to hold buyers' interest, while a buyer who has to guess usually lowers the price.

Helena has many long-time government and school families, so inherited houses come up often. Settle who has legal authority over the estate before you take offers, since that person signs. Court-ordered probate transfers skip the seller disclosure statement, though other estate sales may not, and the title company or an attorney can tell you which case yours is.

Gather the newest tax statement, permit records, notes on the roof, furnace and chimney, and the history of any second unit. When heirs are scattered, settle the lowest acceptable price and the closing date early so no single person stalls the deal. A cash buyer takes the house as is, which suits owners who cannot supervise repairs from far away.

Use the form here to describe the house and a written offer follows. Accepting it sends the file to a title company, which verifies ownership, finds liens and drafts the papers. The closing date can fit your plans. When you close, your mortgage and any unpaid tax go first and you keep the rest. A payoff statement and closing cost estimate at the outset make your net figure clear before you commit.

Cash as is skips the lender's appraisal and the repair requests that tend to follow an inspection. Because condition shapes the price, set the written offer beside what a listing would net once commission and repairs are paid.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit record to sell my Helena house?
faqs.a: Montana's disclosure statement asks about additions made without a building permit. Contact the city's Building Division to check what is on file.

faqs.q: How many accessory dwelling units can I have on a Helena lot?
faqs.a: One. The city code allows one ADU per lot, accessory to a single-dwelling unit residence, and limits it to 75 percent of the main house or 1,000 square feet, whichever is less.

faqs.q: When are Lewis and Clark County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due on November 30, or within 30 days of the postmark if that is later. The second half is due May 31.

faqs.q: Is Helena in a wildfire area?
faqs.a: The city's zoning code says it seeks to minimize danger from wildland fires, so fire exposure is a planning concern, especially on hillsides. Ask your insurer and the city about your specific address.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Helena house that I inherited?
faqs.a: Yes, once the person with legal authority over the estate can sign. Transfers ordered by a probate court are exempt from the seller disclosure statement under section 70-20-503.
